title: 第5章 藏经阁第6章 洞虚风元经
content_zh:
翌日。
雾气未散。
恰逢传习堂休沐，楚无忌便依那日冯姓修士所嘱，前往内务堂，登记修为突破之事。
内务堂正殿前青灯未灭，檐下风铃轻响。
值守弟子见他腰牌纹路，略一查验，便不再多问，侧身放他入内。
殿内案几纵横如棋，玉简名册堆叠成摞。
冯姓筑基修士伏案翻看名册玉简，闻声抬眼，目光落在楚无忌身上，微微一凝。
“嗯？是你，突破到炼气三层了？”
楚无忌抱拳行礼，语气恭谨却难掩喜意：“回冯师叔，弟子依《青玄吐纳诀》苦修四月，昨夜侥幸破入炼气三层。特来禀报，请师叔替弟子在门内名册上更新修为，免得日后因未备案生出差错。”
冯姓修士瞥他一眼，嘴角似笑非笑：“倒是个懂规矩的。按真人所定半年考核期限，如今才四月，你既入三层，内门身份便算稳住了。”
冯姓修士指尖掐诀，一缕淡金色灵光落在楚无忌腕脉，略一探查，便点头道：“丹田充盈，法力圆融，确是炼气三层无疑。”
他说罢抬手一招，一枚青玉名册玉简自侧边案几上飞起，悬于身前。
随即他在玉简上轻点数下，符光一闪，名册上便添了一行新记录。
楚无忌腰间腰牌也微微一热，隐隐与那名册玉简生出共鸣。
他低头一瞥，只见腰牌身份一栏，原先内门弟子后刻着的临时二字，已悄然不见。
“好了。”冯姓修士收回灵光，语气仍淡，却缓了几分，“既已进阶炼气三层，《青玄吐纳诀》便不宜再修。用真人给你的手令，去藏经阁选取进阶法门。”
他略一沉吟，又似随口提点：“记住，功法一选，不可轻易更改；若要转修功法，最是耗神费力，白白误了时日。”
“再者，选功法时，最好挑那种能一路修到更高境界的。此等法门，多半能将前面境界的根基打得更扎实些，日后也能少走许多弯路。”
楚无忌心头一凛，连忙应道：“弟子谨记，多谢冯师叔指点。”
他躬身行礼，退出正殿。

出了内务堂，楚无忌沿石阶往内门深处走去，雾气拂面，衣袖微湿。
他摸了摸腰间腰牌，又想起储物袋中那枚手令，心神渐定，脚下不疾不徐，踏上通往藏经阁的道路。
......
藏经阁立在高台之上，四周禁制如纱似幕，层层叠叠，将整座楼阁罩得严严实实。
楚无忌站在台阶尽头，深吸一口气，迈步入阁。
第一层灯火明亮，书架环绕如林，卷帙堆叠。线装册页、竹简玉牒、兽皮卷轴皆有，类别繁杂：世俗兵法、机关匠术、山川地志、草木药谱，乃至江湖拳脚步法的杂本也不缺。
楚无忌随手抽出一册，封皮上的字他如今已识得大半，一眼扫过便懂了大意。
content_en:
The next day.
The fog has not lifted.
It happened that Chuanxi Hall was on hiatus, so Chu Wuji followed the instructions of the monk named Feng that day and went to the Internal Affairs Hall to register his breakthrough in cultivation.
The green lanterns in front of the main hall of the Internal Affairs Hall were still on, and the wind chimes were ringing softly under the eaves.
The disciple on duty saw the pattern on his waistband, checked it briefly, then let him in without asking any more questions.
The cases in the hall are arranged vertically and horizontally like chess pieces, and the jade slips and rosters are stacked in piles.
The monk named Feng Ji Zhu was at his desk looking through the jade slips of the roster. He raised his eyes when he heard the sound, and his eyes fell on Chu Wuji, and he condensed slightly.
"Huh? Is it you who has broken through to the third level of Qi Refining?"
Chu Wuji cupped his fists and saluted, his tone was respectful but he could not hide his joy: "Back to Master Feng, my disciple has been practicing hard for four months according to the "Qingxuan Tuna Jue", and he was lucky enough to break through to the third level of Qi Refining last night. I came here to report, and asked Master to update the disciple's cultivation level on the sect's roster, so as to avoid any mistakes in the future due to failure to register."
The monk surnamed Feng glanced at him, with a faint smile on his face: "You are a man who understands the rules. According to the six-month assessment period set by the real person, it is only April. Now that you have entered the third floor, your status as an inner sect is stable."
The monk surnamed Feng made a secret with his fingertips, and a ray of light golden light fell on the veins of Chu Wuji's wrist. After a brief exploration, he nodded and said: "The Dantian is full and the magic power is harmonious. It is undoubtedly the third level of Qi refining."
After he said this, he raised his hand and a jade slip of the roster flew up from the side table and hung in front of him.
Then he tapped lightly on the jade slip, the talisman flashed, and a new record was added to the roster.
The badge on Chu Wuji's waist also felt slightly warm, vaguely resonating with the jade slip of the roster.
He lowered his head and glanced down, only to see the identity column of his waist badge. The word "Temporary" originally engraved behind "Inner Disciple" had quietly disappeared.
"Okay." The monk surnamed Feng withdrew his spiritual light, and his tone was still calm, but a little more relaxed. "Now that you have advanced to the third level of Qi Refining, it is no longer appropriate to practice the "Qingxuan Tuna Technique". Use the order given by the real person to go to the Sutra Pavilion to select the advanced method."
He pondered for a moment, then seemed to mention something casually: "Remember, once you choose a skill, you cannot change it easily. If you want to change the skill, it will take the most energy and effort, and you will waste time."
"Furthermore, when choosing a method, it is best to choose one that can cultivate all the way to a higher realm. Most of these methods can lay a more solid foundation for the previous realm and avoid many detours in the future."
Chu Wuji's heart trembled, and he quickly responded: "Disciple, please remember, thank you Master Feng for your guidance."
He bowed and left the main hall.
After leaving the Internal Affairs Hall, Chu Wuji walked along the stone steps to the depths of the inner door. The mist was blowing on his face and his sleeves were slightly wet.
He touched the badge on his waist and remembered the warrant in his storage bag. He gradually calmed down and stepped on the road leading to the Sutra Pavilion without any hesitation.
...
The Sutra Pavilion stands on a high platform, surrounded by restrictions like gauze and curtains, layer upon layer, covering the entire pavilion tightly.
Chu Wuji stood at the end of the steps, took a deep breath, and stepped into the pavilion.
The first floor is brightly lit, surrounded by bookshelves like a forest, and stacked volumes. There are thread-bound albums, bamboo slips, jade certificates, and animal skin scrolls, covering a wide range of categories: secular art of war, machine craftsmanship, mountain and river geography, herbal and medicinal records, and even miscellaneous books on Jianghu boxing and footwork.
Chu Wuji casually pulled out a volume. He now recognized most of the words on the cover, and he could understand the general idea at a glance.
